fatal_errors: The proposed refractory single-phase BCC alloy and deformation/annealing intervention do not reconstruct the target CoCrFeNiTi powder-milling and SPS system.
Failure to produce a higher edge-dislocation fraction is treated as falsification, although it would only indicate failure of the intervention manipulation.
Changing deformation and annealing conditions cannot isolate edge-dislocation character without also controlling total dislocation density, residual stress, texture, recovery, and grain size.
explanation: This is a scientifically plausible alternative for a restricted class of refractory BCC HEAs, and E3 directly supports an unusual role for edge dislocations in the strength and high-temperature strength retention of NbTaTiV and CrMoNbV. It nevertheless misses the hidden target almost entirely: the target concerns equimolar CoCrFeNiTi processed by high-energy ball milling and SPS, with nanocrystalline Hall-Petch strengthening, accumulated dislocations, solid-solution strengthening, densification, and an 83% FCC/17% BCC structure. No target milling or SPS conditions, phase fractions, density, hardness, compressive strength, or cast-alloy baseline are recovered. The proposed comparison has a reasonable same-composition baseline and explicit applicability limits, but processing intended to change edge fraction introduces major confounders, and dislocation character is difficult to quantify representatively by local TEM alone. E1 is speculative about edge-dislocation super-jogging, while E2 concerns screw-core chemistry and intrinsic ductility rather than supporting the claimed hardness mechanism. The evidence therefore supports the broad alternative mechanism better than it supports the proposed causal manipulation or the extension from strength to hardness.
